messages.subject: Variance-Covariance matrix data
parts:
Is there a way to read in a variance-covariance matrix as input data, similar to how MplusAutomation reads in raw data?

Thank you!

-Kiet

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Variance-Covariance matrix data
parts:
Hi
Hear is the commands for variance-covariance as input in mplus
DATA: FILE IS ‘COVARIANCE-MATRIX-FILE-NAME’
TYPE = COVARIANCE;
NOBSERVATIONS = 245; 


bellow is an example from this book

TITLE: PATH ANALYSIS MODEL
DATA: FILE IS EX3.1.COV;
TYPE = COVARIANCE;
NOBSERVATIONS=150;
VARIABLE: NAMES ARE AV_REQRD AV_ELECT SAT IQ ED_MOTIV;
MODEL: AV_REQRD AV_ELECT ON SAT IQ ED_MOTIV;

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Variance-Covariance matrix data
parts:
Hi Kiet,

I'm not sure if I entirely followed your question, but Balal's comment is correct for how one uses a covariance matrix in Mplus. If you're looking to get a covariance matrix into R, you could use read.table() on a txt file. Or if it's the lower triangle of a matrix, check out getCov() in lavaan, which lets you convert from free text covariance to a matrix.

Best,
Michael

messages.author: e379f393de0719fb
messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Variance-Covariance matrix data
parts:
Hi all,

Thank you for your responses. Allow me to clarify my question. This is the syntax I would use in R to fit a confirmatory factor analysis via the MplusAutomation package:

model1 <- mplusObject(
   MODEL = "FA BY X1-X12;",
   OUTPUT = "SAMPSTAT",
   Usevariables = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4", "X5", "X6", "X7", "X8", "X9", "X10", "X11", "X12"),
   rdata = MyData)
   res <- mplusModeler(model1, modelout = "model1.inp", run = 1L)

Typically I would run the model using individual-level data in the "rdata" section (i.e., the MyData would be individual-level input data). How would I adjust this syntax if I wanted to use a variance-covariance matrix instead of individual-level data as the input data?

Thank you,

Kiet
